name: The Wheel — thetagang style (1PercentMax guide)

source.provenance: FetchLayer live pull — post body (841 score) + 243 comments; distilled from the OP guide and the top-voted comment threads.

style_summary: Sell options like an insurance business: collect premium by selling cash-secured puts on quality stocks with elevated implied volatility that you'd be willing to own; if assigned, sell covered calls until the shares are called away. Time entries to mean-reversion — sell puts after a drop, calls after a run.
mechanics: The wheel: sell CSP -> if OTM repeat, if assigned buy 100 shares -> sell CC -> if OTM repeat, if exercised sell shares -> back to CSP.

selection_rules: Elevated implied volatility — author targets IV Rank >= 50 (but see conflict below)
Understand WHY IV is high — skip names facing fraud/bankruptcy/obsolescence (cited failures: WKHS, CCIV)
Liquid underlying AND liquid options — avoid wide bid-ask spreads (low premium doesn't pay for the risk)
Only names you're genuinely willing to own (assignment means holding them)
A diversified basket, never a single ticker; each leg needs >=100x strike in collateral

entry.trigger: Sell CSPs only after the underlying has moved significantly LOWER; sell CCs only after it has moved significantly HIGHER (FA + TA to time the low/high). Sell further OTM on high-IV names to reduce assignment risk.
entry.delta_or_strike: OP gives no delta; a top comment (TacticalYam) uses ~0.30-delta puts in the $25-50 range, with ratio/synthetic structures outside it. [from comments, not the OP]

exit.profit_target: No fixed %. Rule of thumb: the first portion of a sold option decays fast and the last bits slow — once it has lost most of its value, buy it back and sell a new one.
exit.roll_rules: To avoid assignment, roll: buy back the short option and simultaneously sell another, netted for a credit.
exit.assignment_handling: Accept on names you wanted; buy 100 shares and switch to selling covered calls until called away.
exit.stop_or_line_in_sand: Cut and move on if the underlying is fundamentally broken (fraud / failing business), rather than bag-holding. No numeric stop given.

sizing.max_per_underlying: Not stated as a %; rule is 'diversify, >=100x per name, never single-stock'. A commenter (TacticalYam) caps Reg-T buying power at ~60%, more conservative on portfolio margin.
sizing.cash_reserve: CSPs fully cash-secured by default; margin only 'used responsibly' per comments

cadence: Active — monitor the underlying and manage positions; weekly expiries referenced by commenters (one targets ~10% return on capital when assigned).
variants: Hybrid entry (charaZy_freeeK, endorsed by OP): buy 100 shares first, then sell a lower-strike put to average down + a covered call — avoids missing the upside if the stock runs.
High-IV names via ratio spreads / synthetic longs instead of a plain wheel (TacticalYam).
risk_notes: Never wheel a single ticker or a single theme (EV/cannabis/GME) — treat it like YOLO risk.
Don't FOMO into a CSP after a big run-up, or panic-close on unrealized red.
Author's honest caveat: after-tax returns were 'lackluster' vs buy-and-hold SPY; short-term cap-gains; paper trade first.

values: Botboy141 (22 upvotes): high IV NOT mandatory — reasonable returns achievable on low-IV ETFs like SPY; pick IV to match target return/risk
conflicts.resolution: Kept the OP's >=50 IVR as the default but flagged that a well-regarded commenter runs it on low-IV names; organizer to confirm which the community actually follows.

gaps: No explicit profit-target % (only a qualitative 'buy back when most value is gone').
Delta target and margin/BP limits come only from comments, not the OP — confirm they're house rules.
Position count / % per name not quantified in the OP.

disclaimer: Educational tool, not personalized investment advice. The OP explicitly states 'I am not a financial advisor.' Runs on the member's own account with their own risk limits and hold-to-approve execution.
